title: Tutte's theorem on perfect matchings
statement:
Let $G$ be a simple graph on a finite vertex set $V$. For a set $S \subseteq V$, write $G - S$ for the graph obtained by deleting the vertices of $S$ (together with their incident edges), and let $o(G - S)$ denote the number of odd components of $G - S$, that is, the connected components with an odd number of vertices. Then $G$ has a perfect matching if and only if
\[o(G - S) \le \abs{S} \qquad \text{for every } S \subseteq V.\]
hypotheses_covered: the vertex set V is finite
condition quantified over all subsets S of V
odd-component count of G minus S is at most the cardinality of S
